title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the preceding pages treat PGL(2,C) acting on P^1 and the Schwarzian derivative as the basic differential invariant (projective structures on curves). Here Grothendieck runs through the simpler one-dimensional homogeneous spaces in the same 'cocycle/torsor' formalism; the next page goes on to Aff(1).

(a, continued) Translation group G_a acting on E^1. On a smooth complex-analytic curve X, d: O_X -> ω_X is surjective with kernel C, so O_X/C ≅ ω_X. A(f,g) = dg - df is the invariant. If one restricts to the sheaf E_X of étale maps X -> E^1 (local coordinates) instead of all of O_X, df has no zeros. One must then replace ω_X by ω_X^*, the subsheaf of nowhere-vanishing 1-forms (local bases), which is an O_X^*-torsor. The difference dg - df is replaced by the ratio A'(f,g) = dg/df ∈ Γ(X, O_X^*).

(b) G_m acting on E^1 \ {0} ≅ G_m by homotheties. Generalise to an invertible sheaf L with L^* its sheaf of local bases (an O_X^*-torsor); the object of interest is L^*/C^*.
- A local base f determines the unique connection D_f on L with D_f(f) = 0.
- This gives a map D: L^* -> Conn_{X/C}(L), f ↦ D_f. The target is a torsor under ω^1_{X/C}.
- The map is equivariant along dlog: O^* -> ω and induces L^*/C^* ≅ Conn_{X/C}(L). Here dim X = 1 is used: every connection is integrable, so it locally has a horizontal base unique up to C^*.
- Avoiding connections, one defines B(f,g) = d(g/f)/(g/f) = dlog(g/f) ∈ Γ(ω_{X/C}) for f, g ∈ Γ(L^*), playing the role of D_g - D_f. It has cocycle-type properties a)-e) analogous to the Schwarzian ones: cocycle identity, invariance under the group, locality, determination by value at a point, surjectivity.
- For L = O_X, Conn(L) ≅ ω canonically, and g ↦ dg/g gives O_X^*/C^* ≅ ω_{X/C}.

The programme is to show that each (G, X)-structure on a curve (G = G_a, G_m, Aff(1), PGL(2)) corresponds to a torsor under a power or twist of ω, with a canonical differential invariant: dg - df, dg/df, dlog, f''/f', Schwarzian. The next page remarks that success seems tied to the value space being homogeneous under the group (C^* acting on C is 'bad').
errors: Sign/convention: with D_f defined by D_f(f) = 0 one computes D_g - D_f = -dlog(g/f), so B(f,g) = dlog(g/f) equals D_f - D_g. This is harmless up to a convention.
D: L^* -> Conn(L) is called a 'homomorphism', but L^* is a torsor, not a group. It is really an equivariant map over dlog: O^* -> ω.

The isomorphism L^*/C^* ≅ Conn(L), and the surjectivity of dlog, rely on dim X = 1 (or on restricting to integrable connections / closed forms) and on the analytic or étale-local topology. This is implicit, though it was stated for (a) on the previous page.

ideas.what: Sheaf of étale coordinates E_X: ω_X^* is an O^*-torsor and dg/df is the invariant for translation structures with étale charts
ideas.modern_name: translation structures / nowhere-vanishing abelian differentials as (G_a, C)-structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Gunning (1966-78) for the torsor viewpoint

ideas.what: Each local base f of L gives the connection D_f killing f; L^*/C^* ≅ Conn(L), an ω-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Atiyah torsor of connections; flat connections on line bundles over curves; dlog
ideas.where_published: related material in Grothendieck's crystalline/de Rham notes (1966-68), unsure of exact statement

ideas.what: dlog: O^*/C^* ≅ ω on a curve; B(f,g) = dlog(g/f) as a cocycle invariant for G_m-structures
ideas.modern_name: logarithmic derivative as the differential invariant of G_m-structures

ideas.what: Systematic hierarchy G_a, G_m, Aff(1), PGL(2) of 1-dimensional Klein geometries, each with a cocycle invariant valued in a torsor
ideas.modern_name: (G,X)-structures on Riemann surfaces; translation/affine/projective structures as torsors under ω^k
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning, Lectures on Riemann Surfaces (1966); 'On uniformization of complex manifolds' (1978)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard exposition of the torsor/cocycle viewpoint on translation and multiplicative structures on curves. It is essentially Gunning-style theory, preparing the Aff(1) and Schwarzian cases; nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'ε_X' / 'E_X' denotes the sheaf of étale (locally invertible) analytic maps X -> E^1, i.e. local coordinates; Grothendieck's own marginal note on p.74 suggests this notation.
'Dans le cas L = O_X [?]': the reading L = O_X is correct.
The struck-out word 'translation' is replaced by 'homothéties', as transcribed.
